farkle.name: Dice
farkle.text: Six dice: roll, set aside what scores, then decide — risk the rest or bank what you have. Roll nothing that scores and the whole turn is lost. The first to reach the target takes the pot.

liars.name: Liar's Dice
liars.text: Everyone has dice under a cup that only they can see. In turn you bid: “at least four fives on the table” — the next player raises or says “Liar!”. Whoever loses the call loses a die; the last one with dice takes the pot.

poker.name: Dice Poker
poker.text: Five dice and one reroll: keep the best, reroll the rest. A bet before the reroll and one after, hands as in poker — from a pair to five of a kind. The first to win enough hands takes the pot.

kb.name: Knucklebones
kb.text: A duel on two three-by-three boards. Place the rolled die in one of your columns: matching dice in a column multiply, and the same value in your opponent's matching column is knocked out. The game ends when either board is full.

tw.name: Twenty-One
tw.text: Six dice — d4, d6, d8, d10, d12 and d20 — each can be taken once per round. Roll, add, go over the limit and you lose the round. You can stand at any time. The game is played to several round wins.

opt.fewerDice: On a tie, fewer dice wins

scc.name: Ship, Captain and Crew
scc.text: Three rolls of five dice. First you need a ship — a six, then a captain — a five, then a crew — a four. The two remaining dice are your cargo: its total decides who takes the pot.

Rules.title: Rules · {game}
Rules.farkle:
Six dice, two goals — score points and stop in time.

  1. Roll and set aside what scores. No tag-alongs: every die you select must count.
  2. Then decide: roll the rest or bank what you've made this turn.
  3. Roll nothing that scores and it's a bust: the turn's points are lost and play passes on.
  4. Set aside all six and you roll six again and keep going.

{straights} {pairs}

Play to {target}. Your first bank must be at least {entry} in one turn.
Rules.liars:
Everyone has {dice} dice under a cup; only you see your own.

  1. In turn, players bid: “there are at least this many dice of this face on the whole table”.
  2. Each bid must be higher: more dice — or the same number with a higher face.
  3. Instead of bidding you can say “Liar!”. The cups are lifted and counted. If the bid holds, the challenger loses a die; if not, the bidder does.

{wild}

{spot}

No dice — you're out. The last one with dice takes the pot. Whoever lost a die starts the next round.
Rules.poker:
Five dice, one reroll. Everyone's dice are open.

  1. Everyone rolls five dice.
  2. Betting round: check, raise by {raise}, call or fold. At most {maxRaises} raise(s) per round.
  3. Everyone rerolls any of their dice once.
  4. A second betting round and the showdown: the best hand takes it.

Hands, low to high: pair, two pairs, three of a kind, small straight (1–5), big straight (2–6), full house, four of a kind, five of a kind.

Folding gives up only that hand. The game and the whole pot go to the first to win {hands} hand(s).
Rules.kb:
A duel. Each player has a three-by-three board.

  1. On your turn you get a die and place it in one of your columns.
  2. Matching dice in a column multiply: two fours are 16, three are 36.
  3. In your opponent's same column, every die of that value is knocked out.

As soon as either board is full the game ends. The higher total wins.
Rules.tw:
Six dice: d4, d6, d8, d10, d12 and d20. Each can be taken once per round.

  1. On your turn take dice one after another: each roll adds to your total.
  2. Go over {limit} and you bust — the round is lost for you.
  3. You can stand at any time.

The round goes to the highest total that isn't over the limit. {tie} The first seat rotates every round.

The game is played to {wins} round win(s).
Rules.scc:
Five dice and {rolls} rolls per turn.

  1. First you need a six — the ship, then a five — the captain, then a four — the crew. In that order only; anything found in one roll locks in at once.
  2. The two remaining dice are your cargo; their sum is your score.
  3. Once the crew is complete you can reroll the cargo with your remaining rolls or keep it.

No crew — zero. The best cargo takes the pot; ties are replayed between the tied players only.
